comparisons.title: Permits: fewer fields, different questions
comparisons.meaning: The older file includes project valuation, payment, application date and permit status. The newer schema has no equivalent named fields for those concepts. It adds owner and description of work. Application date and issue date describe different events.
comparisons.caution: Different time ranges and workflows; this is a comparison of two editions available now, not proof that columns were deleted from one unchanged item. The old page explicitly links to the newer dataset.

comparisons.title: Parcels: a thinner Q3 2024 edition
comparisons.meaning: The Q3 edition lacks fields such as Owner, total_av and land_av found in Q1. A reader cannot perform the same ownership and valuation analysis using that edition alone.
comparisons.caution: The Q4 2024 edition returns to 69 total fields, including ownership and valuation. This is an uneven series, not a permanent loss of all parcel detail.

comparisons.title: Parcels: ownership and values return
comparisons.meaning: The following quarterly edition restores ownership, assessed values, building characteristics and additional geography fields.
comparisons.caution: Field presence does not establish that every row has a value. No claim about completeness is made from schema counts alone.

comparisons.title: Parcels: a smaller change in the latest edition
comparisons.meaning: The three omitted columns are OBJECTID_1, LATITUDE and LONGITUDE. Polygon geometry is still available, so the missing coordinate columns do not mean that location data disappeared.
comparisons.caution: Counts include identifier and geometry-derived columns. Fewer columns can reflect simplification, not a substantive loss of information.

comparisons.title: Parcels: more columns does not guarantee the same detail
comparisons.meaning: The 2017 schema includes TotTaxOwed, TaxYrsDeli and OverdueWat. Those fields have no direct named counterparts in the latest parcel schema, despite the higher overall field count.
comparisons.caution: These concepts may be available through other city sources. This finding is limited to the compared portal schemas; it is not a citywide claim that tax or water-balance information is unavailable.

comparisons.title: Crime: more explicit columns in later editions
comparisons.meaning: The 2024 Part 1 edition adds explicit LAT, LONG and LarcenyCode columns compared with the archived 2018 edition. DATEEND is a typed date in 2024, compared with a string in the 2018 schema.
comparisons.caution: Both layers have spatial geometry. Additional coordinate columns improve tabular convenience; they do not establish more precise locations. Crime locations are intentionally generalized.

notices.title: Crime Data 2025 Part 1 Offenses With Lat and Long Info
notices.notice: NOTICE : This dataset is not currently updating correctly and does not reflect current Crime Statistics. We hope to get this technical issue resolved shortly. In the interim, please direct all data requests to the Syracuse FOIL team. https://www.syr.gov/Departments/Law/FOIL Dated: 01/30/2026. Description: This 2025 crime data is the list of calls for service that the Syracuse Police Department responded to in 2025. These records does not include rape offenses as well as any crimes that have been sealed by the court. These records are derived from the records management system utilized by the SPD. The data is then anonymized by SPD Crime Analysts weekly. After this data is received weekly from the SPD, this data is then mapped to the approximate location of that incident, using the 100 block level and a Geolocator File from Onondaga County GIS Department. This data is then updated on the Open Data Portal. The points should not be construed to be the exact point this incidents were reported to occur, rather the block where these incident is reported to occur. Crimes are reported to the FBI in two major categories under the Uniform Crime Reports specification: Part 1 and Part 2 crimes. Part 1 crimes include criminal homicide, forcible rape, robbery, aggravated assault, burglary, larceny-theft, and motor vehicle theft. In these records, rape offenses have been excluded due to victim privacy concerns. Part 2 crimes include all other offenses. A more detailed guide to Part 1 crimes is listed below. More details about Part 2 Crimes is listed in the Part 2 Crimes Dataset. When using the data, the date and time provided are when the crime was actually reported. This means that though a larceny might be reported at noon, the actual crime could have happened at 8am, but was not realized until someone noticed hours later. Similarly, if a home break-in happens during a holiday weekend when the owners are out of town, the crime report may not come in until they return home and notice the crime took place previously. The address in the dataset is where the crime occurred. The location is also anonymized to the block level, so a crime that occurred at 123 Main St. will appear as occurring on the 100 block of Main St. This is to protect the privacy of all involved. Finally, information about crimes is fluid, and details about the crime could change.
